_doc: Our additions on top of USDA FoodKeeper. 'names' renames FoodKeeper products (key = FoodKeeper product ID) to the phrase people search for; the slug is derived from the name unless 'slugs' sets one. 'pairs' merges a second FoodKeeper product into a food page as the toggle's second state. 'derived' creates an extra entity whose numbers come from a FoodKeeper product. 'custom' holds entities FoodKeeper does not cover; each MUST carry its own source. 'content' holds hand-written copy keyed by slug and always wins over generated copy. Re-run `npm run data` after editing.

27._why: FoodKeeper lists milk's fridge time only as the package use-by date. FoodSafety.gov's cold food storage chart (USDA/HHS) gives 1 week.

notes.fridge: per FoodSafety.gov chart; or the use-by date

dry.pantry: white rice, sealed; brown rice 1 year

cooked-rice.quote: Cool it within an hour of cooking and reheat to 165°F (74°C) before eating.

methods.note: Do not reheat a second time

signs.title: Smell
signs.text: Sour or musty instead of neutral.

signs.title: Texture
signs.text: Slimy, sticky film or unusually hard, dried grains.

signs.title: Colour
signs.text: Yellow, grey or any green/black spots.

signs.title: Mould
signs.text: Any fuzzy growth — discard the whole container.

freezeSteps: Cool the rice quickly — spread it on a tray so it drops below 40°F within an hour.
Portion into freezer bags, press flat and squeeze the air out; label with the date.
Reheat from frozen with a splash of water, covered, until steaming (165°F).
cooked-rice.leftOut: Rice left at room temperature for more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F) should be thrown away. Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking and produce heat-stable toxins; reheating does not make it safe.

unopened.title: Dry, unopened
unopened.text: FoodKeeper gives dry white rice 2 years in the pantry and brown rice 1 year — the oils in brown rice go rancid. Keep it sealed, cool and dry.

opened.title: Cooked
opened.text: There is no printed date; the clock starts when it cools. Count 4–6 days from the day you cooked it, not from the day you bought the rice.

store: Refrigerate within 1 hour in a shallow, airtight container.
Keep the fridge at or below 40°F (4°C); the door shelf is warmest.
Reheat only the portion you will eat; do not reheat more than once.
faq: How long can cooked rice sit out?
No more than 2 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour when it is above 90°F. After that, discard it.
Is week-old rice safe?
No. The USDA window is 4–6 days refrigerated. At 7 days, throw it away even if it looks fine.
Can I reheat rice twice?
Reheat only once, to 165°F, and only the portion you will eat.
Does brown rice last as long as white?
Cooked, both keep 4–6 days. Dry brown rice goes rancid in about a year; dry white rice keeps about 2 years.
Why is leftover rice risky?
Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking and multiply at room temperature, producing toxins that reheating does not destroy.
How do I cool rice fast?
Spread it on a sheet pan or divide into shallow containers so it drops below 40°F within an hour.

eggs.leftOut: Refrigerated eggs left out more than 2 hours should be discarded. A cold egg left out can sweat, which lets bacteria move through the shell. In the US, eggs are washed, so they must stay refrigerated.
faq: Do eggs go bad in the fridge?
Yes, slowly. In-shell eggs keep 3–5 weeks after purchase at 40°F or below. The sell-by date may pass during that time.
Does the float test work?
It shows age, not safety. An old egg floats because its air cell grows. Crack it into a bowl and check the smell.
Can you freeze eggs in the shell?
No. The contents expand and crack the shell. Beat them first, then freeze for up to 12 months.
How long do hard-boiled eggs last?
1 week in the fridge, peeled or unpeeled.

salmon.quote: FoodKeeper groups salmon with other fatty fish, such as tuna, mackerel and catfish.

liquor.quote: This covers unflavoured spirits such as vodka, tequila, gin, rum and whiskey.

mashed-potatoes.quote: FoodKeeper counts mashed potatoes as leftovers without meat. Homemade mash with cream or butter follows the same 3–4 day rule.

splits._doc: FoodKeeper records that name several foods. Each listed food gets its own page with the record's exact numbers; the page says which USDA group it belongs to. Only foods FoodKeeper names explicitly.
